key_insight: Quantum circuit simulation cost is strongly family-dependent, and a family-aware residual neural model can predict both required approximation threshold and runtime from OpenQASM and context.
engineering_relevance: This can replace slow trial-and-error tuning for approximate tensor-network simulators, helping practitioners choose simulation settings in milliseconds instead of minutes or hours.
method: Shared neural backbone reads circuit and execution-context features.
Pretrained family classifier adds algorithm-family context for residual corrections.
Family-specific additive residuals refine predictions using gate-composition fingerprint features.
evidence_signal: Across 7–130 qubit circuits from 10 algorithm families, the model reached 79.5% exact threshold accuracy, 91.2% within one rung, and runtime prediction with R² = 0.82, with ~50 ms inference.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reliable family classification and representative training coverage; unseen circuit families or atypical entanglement patterns could reduce accuracy.
paper_title: Family-Aware Residual Architecture for Predicting Quantum Circuit Simulation Performance
